The study applies XGBoost classification to predict volleyball performance using pre-season Fitbit data and EMA surveys. Key features include HRV, breathing rate, and sedentary time. The model achieves highest F1 score (0.7549) during Phase 2+3, suggesting optimal training adaptation windows. However, the small sample size (N=14) introduces high variance and potential confounding by position. The binarized outcome (hit % > 0.2) limits generalizability to other domains like NFL. The method's reliance on wearable data and EMA precludes direct application to GSE without substantial re-engineering due to domain mismatch and lack of access to such telemetry.
